about: One plain-language line per hypothesis, shown on the results page above its folded details (#893). Each restates the hypothesis heading in docs/research/plan.md and adds nothing to it; the plan decides. Draft by the orchestrating session for Eleonora's review. scripts/research_view.py refuses a plan hypothesis without a line here, and a line for a hypothesis the plan does not have.

taglines.H1: The scorer puts forecasts of known quality in the right order.
taglines.H2: The data already held carries signal for the spread and for pressure on ordinary days.
taglines.H4: A longer history fixes part of the 2018–19 misses.
taglines.H5: A forecast of the whole range of the SOFR − IORB spread, in basis points, beats the phase 2 models and the yes-or-no pressure forecasts.
taglines.H6: The spread on known risk dates, such as settlements, tax days and month- and quarter-ends, can be forecast.
taglines.H7: Reserve scarcity can be tracked directly, as a slow-moving state.
taglines.H8: For desks, ranking the next 20 business days by risk beats calibrating probabilities.
taglines.H9: Richer targets, such as the SOFR tail, other repo rates and take-up at the Fed's facilities, hold more signal a model can learn.
taglines.H10: Each pressure episode can be traced to its drivers.
